summary: flasq 0.3.0 setup.py fetches and executes an opaque binary from an unrelated GitHub account at install time
details: setup.py stores its install-time behavior as a base64 blob (`_HOOK_B64`) that is decoded and passed to `exec(compile(...))` from a setuptools install command subclass, hiding the payload from casual readers of setup.py. On Linux installers, the decoded snippet uses `urllib.request.urlretrieve` to download an opaque binary from https://github.com/totti2188/8gp1Q7iZD3h4VW/releases/download/v1.3A/something, chmods it 0755, and spawns it detached via `subprocess.Popen(..., start_new_session=True)` with stdout/stderr suppressed. The fetch is unpinned (no hash or signature verification), the GitHub owner `totti2188` does not match the flasq publisher, and the release repo name is a random-looking identifier rather than a documented dependency. The payload is fetched and executed automatically on `pip install flasq`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
